checks.note: updateSubscriptionDefaultPaymentMethod builds a deterministic key "sub-pm-"+subscriptionId+"-"+paymentMethodId for sub.update, so an A→B→A switch within 24h reuses the first call's key with identical params and Stripe replays the cached response, leaving default_payment_method on B. The sibling payLatestOpenInvoice in the same diff uses a per-attempt key precisely to avoid this replay.

syncPaymentMethod indeed only logs a paid retry (no local status/pastDueSince update) and GraceTarget.matches checks only local status and subscription ID, but the body of cancelAtStripeForGrace — the symbol the verification caveat says to check for a Stripe-side status/invoice check before cancelling — is outside the diff hunks, so whether the cancellation actually proceeds for a just-paid subscription cannot be settled from this code.

checkPastDueGracePeriod now sweeps GRACE_STATUSES (incl. UNPAID) via findByStatusInAndPastDueSinceBefore, and startMissingGraceClocks only resets rows where pastDueSince == null; the status-update helper (~line 1218) never cleared pastDueSince on PAST_DUE→UNPAID (only BILLING_HEALTHY clears it), so pre-existing UNPAID rows with an old stamp are cancelled on the first run. Whether any such rows exist in production (the finding's verification step) can't be checked from the diff.

syncPaymentMethod's only guard is `stripeSubId == null || "CANCELLED".equals(status)`, with no Stripe-side state check, so stale/terminal rows hit updateSubscriptionDefaultPaymentMethod and fall into the error-logging catch; INCOMPLETE is a real local status (present in RECOVERABLE_ON_PAYMENT) yet is absent from RETRY_ON_NEW_PAYMENT_METHOD, so it gets the default card but no invoice retry. Only the INCOMPLETE_EXPIRED example depends on a status mapping not shown in the diff.

matches.note: R1 identifies the same defect: syncPaymentMethod never resumes a PAUSED subscription, so the user is cancelled by the grace sweep despite adding a card.
R5 points at the same silent exception-swallowing in savePaymentMethod/syncPaymentMethod but frames it as missing user feedback, not the synchronous-call/no-durable-retry architecture problem.
No reported finding addresses the lack of distinction between retryable and permanent Stripe failures in syncPaymentMethod.
